lines.name: Sacramento Northern trains, San Francisco to Bay Point and Sacramento
lines.summary: Electric trains from the Key Route pier, and from 1939 the Bay Bridge, by 40th St and Shafter Ave in Oakland, through the hills by Shepherd Canyon and the Redwood Peak tunnel, to Moraga, Walnut Creek, Concord and Bay Point, and from September 1913 on by West Pittsburg, the train ferry from Mallard to Chipps Island, Montezuma and Rio Vista Junction to Sacramento, until 1940. Drawn to the Yolo County line, where it leaves the Bay Area (decision 16).
lines.fate_note: Replaced by Pacific Greyhound buses in 1941 (CRC Decision No. 34232). Freight trains used the line through the Oakland hills until 1957.

route.note: Over the Key Route's pier to its ferries until January 15, 1939
Over the Key Route's tracks on 40th St

Trains north of West Pittsburg ended on or about August 1940: the Railroad Commission's Decision No. 33416 of August 20, 1940 let them stop on five days' notice, effective five days from its date; the last day isn't sourced (decision 17)

By the train ferry across Suisun Bay. Trains north of West Pittsburg ended on or about August 1940: the Railroad Commission's Decision No. 33416 of August 20, 1940 let them stop on five days' notice, effective five days from its date; the last day isn't sourced (decision 17)

sources.note: "Regular through train service from San Francisco to Bay Point was inaugurated on April 7."
"On April 7 the last-named company expected to inaugurate regular train service between Oakland and Bay Point" (p. 726).
Train service over the bridge from January 15, 1939.
Authorizes ending "passenger train service between the City and County of San Francisco and Pittsburg" (May 27, 1941).
"the last day of regular service on the Sacramento Northern Railway, June 30, 1941" (a reminiscence)
The first through train from Sacramento to Oakland ran on July 2, 1913.
"On that day [September 3, 1913] the schedule of eight trains daily between Sacramento and San Francisco became effective."
Passenger trains north of West Pittsburg may stop "on July 30, 1940, unless sooner expressly permitted".
Authorizes the Sacramento Northern "to abandon its passenger train service between West Pittsburg and Sacramento" on five days' notice (August 20, 1940).

lines.notes: The last day, June 30, 1941, rests on a railfan magazine's reminiscence of 1945; the Railroad Commission authorized the end in May 1941. Through service to Sacramento, by the Chipps Island ferry, ran from September 3, 1913 (the first through train on July 2) to on or about August 1940 (Decision No. 33416); after that the trains ran to Pittsburg. The Pittsburg branch itself isn't drawn yet: its opening isn't sourced.

lines.name: Sacramento Northern freight, Oakland to West Lafayette
lines.summary: The Sacramento Northern's line from 40th St and Shafter Ave, Oakland, through the Oakland hills tunnel, Canyon and Moraga to West Lafayette, after its passenger trains ended in 1941: freight only, until the Western Pacific gave it up in 1957 (decision 15).
lines.fate_note: The Interstate Commerce Commission let the line be abandoned on July 3, 1956 (Finance Docket 19124), and it was abandoned as of March 1, 1957, when the Oakland Terminal's Union St line opened; the track and wire were sold for scrap on March 28. East of West Lafayette the line stayed in use.

route.note: The street track in Shafter Ave went with the rest.
The abandonment ended at West Lafayette station, a little short of Lafayette, whose place no source here gives; this segment runs on to Lafayette, which stayed in use.

sources.note: The last day of the passenger trains, June 30, 1941.
"since then the Sacramento Northern has been used only for freight"; about 16 miles between 40th and Shafter and West Lafayette station.
The application to abandon "about 17.52 miles of line in Oakland and West Lafayette" (Finance Docket 19124).
Finance Docket 19124 granted by Division 4, July 3, 1956.
The Union St line opened on March 1, 1957; the SN "saw its last operation to West Layfette" (sic).
"abandoned by Western Pacific as of March 1".

lines.notes: Its years as a freight line begin with the passenger trains' last day; the line carried freight before that too. The last freight train's day isn't sourced (pointers say February 28, 1957). The sources give its length as 15.52, 16, 17.52 and 18 miles.
